**Finding submitted: T4C — missing (high severity)**

**What I found.** Article IV (p0049) locks Licensee into a 36-month Initial Period, renewable for a further seven years *at Licensor's option*. Sweeping the rest of the document (Article XIX Insolvency, Article XX Certain Other Events of Termination, Article XXI Effect of Termination, Article XXIII Non-Exclusive Remedy), there is **no Licensee right to terminate without cause** anywhere. Termination rights run almost entirely one way:

- Licensor may terminate **immediately** on *any* breach by Licensee of any representation, warranty, covenant or obligation (p0049), and on breach of the licence restrictions (p0043, p0049).
- Licensor may terminate on Licensee's wind-up (p0137), and the Agreement auto-terminates on a Licensee Change of Control absent Licensor consent (p0134).
- On termination for any reason, Licensee must return all Licensed Technology within 5 days and all Licensor rights survive (p0138) — with no refund mechanic at all.

On the positive side, Licensor has no express convenience-termination right either, so the walk-away trigger on that limb isn't hit; the gap is purely the absent Customer exit in a multi-year term.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** A new Article IV paragraph "IV" inserted after p0049 giving Licensee convenience termination on thirty (30) days' notice, in whole or in part, without penalty, with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirming Licensor has no convenience exit during the Initial Period or any extension.

**Negotiation posture.** The comment flags the fallback up front — 60–90 days' notice plus an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees — since a licensor pricing a 36-month amortisation may resist a bare 30-day exit. Worth noting for the broader negotiation: our exit right is materially less valuable while Licensor holds unilateral immediate termination on *any* breach with no cure period, and while Article XXI provides no refund of prepaid fees on a Licensor-initiated termination. Those sit under separate rules but compound this one.
